title: Sweet Georgia Brown
composer: Ben Bernie / Maceo Pinkard / Kenneth Casey
origin: American jazz-age standard, published 1925; the archetypal dominant-cycle jam tune, a fixture of trad-jazz, swing, and jam-session repertoire ever since

pd.detail: First published 1925 by Jerome H. Remick & Co., New York. Words and music credited to Ben Bernie, Maceo Pinkard, and Kenneth Casey.
pd.sourceEdition: The standard published changes of the 1925 composition as fixed in common jam practice; encoded from the harmonic scheme, not from any recorded performance or later copyrighted arrangement.
pd.notes: CHART ONLY: changes and form, no melody and no lyrics. The 1925 sheet is felt in two (cut time); encoded here as 4/4 at half the written pulse. One simplification for the one-chord-per-bar grid: the final phrase's two-chord bar (Bb7 Eb7) is compressed to Eb7, keeping the V7-I cadence; everything else already moves on barlines.

notes: Thirty-two-bar form built from four-bar dominant plateaus cycling home: F7 (VI7) for four, Bb7 (II7) for four, Eb7 (V7) for four, then Ab (I) for four. The second half repeats the F7 and Bb7 plateaus, detours to the relative minor (Fm alternating with its dominant C7 by bar), and cadences Ab - F7 - Eb7 - Ab. The 'a' section is shared by both halves of the chorus, so the form references it twice. Intro and outro are chord-only turnaround vamps built from the tune's own cadence material -- arrangement, not composition. Jam note: the long single-chord plateaus are the point; solos ride each dominant for four full bars before the cycle turns.
